packageRules.description: From v2 on, a new major version of a Go module has a new module path, so a major update of an indirect requirement swaps a path the dependencies import for one nothing imports. go mod tidy puts the old path back and the pull request can never pass. An indirect requirement moves to a new major path only when a direct dependency starts importing it, and that dependency's update brings it in. Majors that keep the path, v0 to v1 and +incompatible, are turned off too and arrive the same way, with the direct dependency that needs them. This rule comes after the one enabling indirect updates so it wins

Kubernetes' modules move together, and k8s.io/kube-openapi's master often breaks the latest Kubernetes release until the next one ships, so they get a pull request of their own that can stay red without holding back every other update. This rule comes after the patch and minor rules so its group wins
The requirements between humus modules name the last release and are set only by the release workflow, so Renovate leaves them alone
The minimum Go version in go.mod follows a support schedule, so it is bumped by hand
